rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before real data; a shared-field coefficient (c_x) added before real data because the HH's kill was ill-posed; synthetic validation on real presence grids (estimator recovery, null size and power, b ~ 2 from private burstiness); 70-unit replication on four channels, raw and trimmed; two natives (NE14, NE43); cross-checks with H38 and H54; scorecard; frozen, guarded confirm script dry-run, not run. Gauge written per unit (1,643 rows). No holdout run; no lagged split of c_x.
rationale.faithfulness: The HH's Taylor premise fails: across agents b ~ 0.85 and c_T <= 0, so c_T and b are not field gauges. The pair-covariance coefficient behaves as a shared-field gauge: small (0.008 trimmed; phi 0.08), 77% removed by trimming in regime III (H38's 70-80%), unchanged by operator drives (NE43), larger for talk than activity (H50). Per-unit agreement with H38's f_scaffold fails, NE14's raw clause fails, and c_x does not separate field from equal-time coupling. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: Gives every hypothesis a one-number shared-field gauge per unit (taylor_c_shared, activity_trim/raw; taylor_phi_shared) in per_period_estimates, says ~90% of activity's excess variance is private, and warns not to use Taylor b or c_T as field measures in clocked agent swarms. Raw-minus-trimmed c_x flags village-off gaps.
